sections.html:
Normal is a town in McLean County, central Illinois, and forms the Bloomington-Normal pair with its neighbor Bloomington. Population is 53,275 (July 1, 2025 estimate). Illinois State University and Heartland Community College shape the market: only 54.8% of homes are owner-occupied, the median owner-occupied value is $213,600, median gross rent is $965, and 75.5% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier. Rentals are a normal part of the market, so the town's rules for rental licenses and short-term stays come up in many sales.

Uptown Normal, built around a roundabout, holds the town hall, the Amtrak station and the restored Normal Theater. The average trip to work takes 16.5 minutes.

Multi-family rentals need a license. Section 11.8-1 of the Town code says no one may operate an apartment, rooming house, multiple-use dwelling, hotel, motel, bed and breakfast or duplex (except the owner-occupied side) without a rental occupancy license issued by the Building Commissioner.

  • Licenses run January 1 through December 31 of a year.
  • A license belongs to one owner and one property and cannot be transferred without a transfer fee and a completed application from the new owner.
  • A change of owner is one reason a license may be revoked.
  • An inspection takes place before any license is issued, and the owner must give the Town access to the units. A tenant or owner who refuses can face a search warrant request.
  • Appeals of a refusal or revocation go to the Building Commissioner within 30 days.
  • Penalties run from $25 to $200 for a first offense and $50 to $500 for later ones, with each day counted as a separate offense.

If you are selling a duplex or small apartment building, tell the buyer that the license does not move with the deed. The Inspections Department is at 1 Uptown Circle, phone 309-454-9581.

Short-term rentals in Normal need a Town business license, under Ordinance 6028 passed on June 16, 2025. They are prohibited in R-1 and R-2 zoning unless the property is the owner-occupant's primary residence.

  • In R-1 zoning, no more than 2 unrelated people, or 1 family plus 1 unrelated person, may stay.
  • In R-2 and R-3 zoning, the limit is 4 unrelated people.
  • Parking is allowed only on hard surfaces, and street parking is capped at 24 hours unless a sign says otherwise.
  • Parties, meetings and other events are not allowed.
  • The Short-Term Rental Tax form and payment are due by the 25th of the month after collection.

The business license carries no fee, but the Town issues it only after taxes and debts owed to the Town are paid. If the house has been used as a short-term rental, ask the Town how the license and any tax account will be handled so the buyer does not inherit a balance.

sections.h2: Recording a deed in McLean County
sections.html:
The McLean County Clerk's Recording Division records deeds at 115 E. Washington Street, Room M104, in Bloomington. The phone is 309-888-5170 and the office is open Monday through Friday, 8 am to 4:30 pm.

Every deed must include:

  • A statement of exemption or a transfer tax declaration.
  • The name of the person who prepared it.
  • Where future tax statements are to be sent.
  • A notary seal, date and signature, with original signatures. Photocopies and digital signatures are not accepted.
  • A complete legal description with the permanent index number.
  • A complete return address.

Staff cannot give legal advice or legal descriptions, so have the deed prepared by an attorney or title company.

Rivian builds all-electric vehicles at the former Diamond-Star Motors plant in Normal, its largest in the United States, which has changed the local job picture. Interstates 55, 74 and 39 serve the town, and U.S. 51, U.S. 150, Illinois Route 9 and historic Route 66 pass through. The Amtrak station at 11 Uptown Circle has four Lincoln Service trains a day in each direction between Chicago and St. Louis, and Connect Transit runs 16 fixed routes.

The town sits inside McLean County Unit District No. 5, which runs Normal Community High School, Normal Community West High School and Kingsley Junior High School. Illinois State University operates University High School and Thomas Metcalf Elementary. Private options include Epiphany Catholic School, Calvary Christian Academy, Cornerstone Christian Academy and Bloom Community School.

Normal gets about 39.4 inches of precipitation and 20.1 inches of snow a year. July highs average 86 degrees Fahrenheit and January lows about 16. That range is hard on roofs, gutters, window seals and furnaces. If your house is older, a recent roof receipt or a furnace service record answers some of the first questions a buyer's inspector will ask.

Work through the sale in this order. First decide how to sell: an agent for a house that shows well, or a cash buyer if repairs, tenants or a license problem would slow a normal listing. Second, if the property is a rental, call the Inspections Department at 309-454-9581 about the license and the transfer fee the buyer will face. Third, have an attorney or title company prepare the deed to the county's list, with original notarized signatures and the permanent index number.

Finally, record the deed with the McLean County Clerk and keep the recorded copy. Before closing, ask the Town whether any short-term rental tax account or other balance is open, since the Town issues licenses only after debts are paid.

A cash sale skips showings, appraisal and lender timelines, but the license, tax and recording steps above stay the same.

sections.h2: Which license does your property need?
sections.html:
Licenses that can affect a Normal sale
Property useLicense neededWhat happens at sale
Apartment, duplex or other multi-family rentalRental occupancy license from the Building CommissionerDoes not transfer without a fee and a new application from the buyer
Short-term rentalTown business licenseIssued only after taxes and debts owed to the Town are paid

If neither applies, because the house is owner-occupied or rented only under normal long-term arrangements outside these categories, the license questions drop away and the sale is mostly deed, title and closing paperwork. When you are unsure which category your property falls in, phone the Inspections Department at 309-454-9581 before listing. A clear answer in writing helps a buyer's lender and attorney, and it keeps a surprise from appearing in the last week before closing.

Buyers who plan to rent the house will ask the same question, so have the answer ready in the first conversation rather than the last.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Normal rental property to another landlord?
faqs.a: Yes. The rental occupancy license is specific to one owner and one property, so the buyer applies in their own name, pays a transfer fee and passes an inspection. Ask the Inspections Department at 309-454-9581 how that will be handled before closing.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a Normal house?
faqs.a: At the McLean County Clerk's Recording Division, 115 E. Washington Street, Room M104, Bloomington, phone 309-888-5170. The deed needs a transfer tax declaration or exemption statement, original notarized signatures and a full legal description with the permanent index number.

faqs.q: Are short-term rentals allowed in Normal?
faqs.a: They are allowed with a Town business license, but not in R-1 or R-2 zoning unless the property is the owner's primary residence. Guest limits depend on the zoning district.

faqs.q: What are typical home values in Normal?
faqs.a: The median value of an owner-occupied home is $213,600. The town has a 54.8% owner-occupied rate, a $965 median gross rent and a median household income of $64,785.

faqs.q: How long is the commute from Normal to work?
faqs.a: The mean trip to work is 16.5 minutes. Interstates 55, 74 and 39 serve the town, and Connect Transit runs 16 fixed routes.
